text.p: Heatwave conditions may result in problems in the Eastern USA through midweek. High temperatures will be in the 90sF along most of the East Coast. A back-door cold front may provide temporary relief in the New England coastal areas during today as winds come in from the cooler Atlantic. High temperatures of 95-100F are expected in Washington DC. Heat-related problems are likely, especially in that region. High heat will also continue in the Plains this period.

The tropics are active in the eastern Pacific and Atlantic, but the threats are mostly to shipping at this time. Hurricane Enrique is about 1150 miles southwest of Baja in the eastern Pacific, and moving northwest. Top winds have peaked at 105 mph and are expected to begin to weaken. Tropical Depression 08E, with 35 mph winds, is about 830 miles south of Baja California, moving west. It is expected to strengthen into a tropical storm but remain over open water. Tropical Storm Claudette, with 40 mph winds, is 200 miles east of Cape Hatteras, NC, in the Atlantic, and is expected to move northeast during today.
There are no further statements at this time.
